  phase with maximal total-variation separation. Infinite-support projective mixtures form the

Join local support geometry, global convex/dynamical phase, metric separation, and reconstruction

## Proof

**[PROVED HERE]** Fix a normalized positive moment form with bounded kernel and let `F` be its
canonical boundary family. For each real parameter `t`, barycentring the projective Dirac law at
`t` gives `F.leaf(t)`, definitionally the constructed `nevLeaf(t)`. The Dirac characterization of
stationary ergodicity and the Bauer extreme-point characterization therefore make this carrier both
ergodic and extreme.

For every compact real observation window `K`, the finite-denominator-fibre theorem supplies a
finite `A ⊆ K` on which restriction of `nevLeaf(t)` is already exact. Thus every pure real leaf is
locally finite on compacts. For distinct real parameters `t,u`, their denominator fibres are
disjoint and measurable, so the corresponding probability leaves are mutually singular. The
total variation of their signed difference on the whole line is therefore exactly two.

Now take an infinite-support projective parameter law. The existing ergodic/extreme/frame phase
theorem says its barycentric carrier has infinite real support, is neither stationary-ergodic nor
extreme, and its complete inverse-Cholesky frame tower uniquely recovers the parameter law among
all infinite-support laws.

Hence pure real leaves and infinite-support mixtures occupy sharply different local-support,
ergodic, convex, and metric phases, while the mixed phase remains globally identifiable. No
computation is used. ∎

## Theorem `[PROVED HERE]`

Let
\[

 0,&e\geq1,

\]
on prime-power coordinates \((p,e)\).  Let \(\mathcal A_{\rm fin}\) be profiles active on only
finitely many prime rays and \(\mathcal Q=\mathcal A/\mathcal A_{\rm fin}\).

1. \([d]\ne0\) in \(\mathcal Q\).
2. For every \(u\ne0\), \(d\) is not supported on the phase-node locus
   \(\sin(u(e+1)\log p)=0\).
3. Consequently no scalar phase-node prime-power source, including an infinite one-prime tower,
   represents the canonical Route E depth-zero current in the global prime-clock quotient.

## Proof

The exact Route E/Gamma depth-zero reduction gives
\[
d(p,0)=p^{-1/2}>0
\]
for every rational prime \(p\).  Hence every prime ray is active.  The prime set is infinite, so
\(d\notin\mathcal A_{\rm fin}\), proving \([d]\ne0\).

Suppose \(u\ne0\) and every active coordinate of \(d\) were a phase node.  The arithmetic
phase-node theorem says active prime-base support is subsingleton: if distinct primes \(p,q\)
were active, then
\[
u\log p=m\pi,\qquad u\log q=n\pi
\]
would produce a nontrivial integer-linear relation between \(\log p\) and \(\log q\), contradicting
unique factorization.  But \(d(p,0)\ne0\) for every prime, contradiction.  Equivalently, the
updated prime-clock quotient theorem puts every phase-node prime-power profile in
\(\mathcal A_{\rm fin}\), whereas \(d\) is not local.

/-!
# Canonical local Brauer characters for the rational adelic route

The Connes--Tate local source cannot factor through an additive complex-valued Brauer observable:
such an observable is forced to vanish.  If the expected local Brauer invariant is supplied,
however, composing it with the canonical circle character of `ℚ/ℤ` gives a faithful nonlinear
local phase.  This is the available ABHN-side carrier for a future comparison with a Tate local
factor.

No equality with the Connes--Tate local zeta integral is claimed here.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower

open IsDedekindDomain Rat.HeightOneSpectrum
open GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.ABHN

noncomputable section

/-- The faithful complex phase obtained by composing a supplied local Brauer invariant with the
canonical circle character of `ℚ/ℤ`. -/
noncomputable def ccmRationalLocalBrauerStdAddChar
    (v : HeightOneSpectrum ℤ)
    (invariant : BrauerGroup ℚ_[Rat.HeightOneSpectrum.primesEquiv v] ≃+ RatModInt) :
    AddChar (BrauerGroup (CCMRationalLocalField v)) ℂ :=
  ratModIntStdAddChar.compAddMonoidHom
    (ccmRationalLocalInvariantAddEquivOfPadic v invariant).toAddMonoidHom

/-- A supplied local invariant makes the canonical local Brauer phase faithful. -/
theorem ccmRationalLocalBrauerStdAddChar_injective
    (v : HeightOneSpectrum ℤ)
    (invariant : BrauerGroup ℚ_[Rat.HeightOneSpectrum.primesEquiv v] ≃+ RatModInt) :
    Function.Injective (ccmRationalLocalBrauerStdAddChar v invariant) := by
  exact ratModIntStdAddChar_injective.comp
    (ccmRationalLocalInvariantAddEquivOfPadic v invariant).injective

/-- The canonical local Brauer phase is one exactly for the split Brauer class. -/
theorem ccmRationalLocalBrauerStdAddChar_eq_one_iff_eq_zero
    (v : HeightOneSpectrum ℤ)
    (invariant : BrauerGroup ℚ_[Rat.HeightOneSpectrum.primesEquiv v] ≃+ RatModInt)
    (x : BrauerGroup (CCMRationalLocalField v)) :
    ccmRationalLocalBrauerStdAddChar v invariant x = 1 ↔ x = 0 := by
  constructor
  · intro hx
    apply ccmRationalLocalBrauerStdAddChar_injective v invariant
    rw [hx]
    exact (ccmRationalLocalBrauerStdAddChar v invariant).map_zero_eq_one.symm
  · intro hx
    rw [hx]
    exact (ccmRationalLocalBrauerStdAddChar v invariant).map_zero_eq_one

/-- A nonsplit local Brauer class has a nontrivial canonical phase. -/
theorem ccmRationalLocalBrauerStdAddChar_ne_one_of_ne_zero
    (v : HeightOneSpectrum ℤ)
    (invariant : BrauerGroup ℚ_[Rat.HeightOneSpectrum.primesEquiv v] ≃+ RatModInt)
    (x : BrauerGroup (CCMRationalLocalField v)) (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    ccmRationalLocalBrauerStdAddChar v invariant x ≠ 1 := by
  intro hchar
  exact hx (ccmRationalLocalBrauerStdAddChar_eq_one_iff_eq_zero v invariant x |>.mp hchar)

end

    (P : Finset Nat.Primes) (A m k : ℝ) :
    xiPhysicalPrimeLogAggregateApertureCarrier P A m k =

        xiPhysicalEndpointResponseRemainderApertureCarrier P A m k := by
  have h := xiPhysicalPrimeLogAggregate_add_fusedResponse_eq_remainder P A m k

/-- The trace-class remainder carrier has norm at most `√A` times the summable remainder weight sum:

    (P : Finset Nat.Primes) :

      ≤ Real.sqrt A * ∑ p ∈ P, xiPhysicalEndpointResponseWeightRemainder p := by
  rw [xiPhysicalEndpointResponseRemainderApertureCarrier]

          xiPhysicalPrimeLogCenteredApertureCarrier A m k p‖
      ≤ ∑ p ∈ P, ‖xiPhysicalEndpointResponseWeightRemainder p •
          xiPhysicalPrimeLogCenteredApertureCarrier A m k p‖ := norm_sum_le _ _
    _ = ∑ p ∈ P, xiPhysicalEndpointResponseWeightRemainder p *
          ‖xiPhysicalPrimeLogCenteredApertureCarrier A m k p‖ := by
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl; intro p _
        rw [norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs,
          abs_of_nonneg (xiPhysicalEndpointResponseWeightRemainder_pos p).le]

          (xiPhysicalEndpointResponseWeightRemainder_pos p).le
    _ = Real.sqrt A * ∑ p ∈ P, xiPhysicalEndpointResponseWeightRemainder p := by
